# useBroadcastChannel

> Typed messages between same-origin tabs, windows and workers via BroadcastChannel.

🟡 intermediate · React 18.0+ · Custom Hooks › Storage & persistence · support: browser-limited

**Playground:** `npm run dev` → [`#/entry/use-broadcast-channel`](http://localhost:5173/#/entry/use-broadcast-channel)

## Concept

Opens a `BroadcastChannel` in an effect, delivers incoming messages to the latest `onMessage` (and `lastMessage`), and closes the channel on unmount or name change.

## Problem

Tabs need to coordinate — log out everywhere, refresh after a change elsewhere — without a server round-trip or abusing the `storage` event.

## When to use

- Event-style notifications: logout, “cart changed”, “new version deployed, reload”.
- Coordinating workers or iframes on the same origin.

## When not to use

- State that new tabs must see — messages are not persisted (use `useLocalStorage` or `useCrossTabState`).
- Cross-origin communication — use `window.postMessage` with origin checks.
- Secrets: any same-origin script can join the channel.

## API

```ts
function useBroadcastChannel<T>(
  name: string | null,
  options?: {
    onMessage?: (message: T, event: MessageEvent) => void;
    validate?: (data: unknown) => data is T;
    onError?: (error: Error) => void;
  },
): { isSupported: boolean; postMessage: (message: T) => boolean; lastMessage: T | undefined };
```

| Parameter                        | Type                       | Description                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                           | `string \| null`           | Channel name; `null` disconnects.                              |
| `options.onMessage` _(optional)_ | `(message, event) => void` | Latest handler is always called.                               |
| `options.validate` _(optional)_  | `(data) => data is T`      | Guards against messages from older app versions in other tabs. |
| `options.onError` _(optional)_   | `(error) => void`          | `DataCloneError`, `messageerror` and failed validation.        |

**Returns:** `isSupported`, a stable `postMessage` (returns `false` when it could not send) and `lastMessage`.

## Execution flow

1. Render: `isSupported` comes from `useSyncExternalStore` (server snapshot `false`), avoiding hydration mismatches.
2. Effect: a channel is created and `message`/`messageerror` listeners attached.
3. Cleanup: listeners removed and `channel.close()` called.

## Common mistakes

### Expecting your own messages

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
channel.postMessage('ping'); // waiting for it in the same instance
```

A BroadcastChannel never delivers a message to the instance that sent it — only to other instances.

### Forgetting to close

❌ Incorrect:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const channel = new BroadcastChannel('app');
  channel.onmessage = handle;
}, []);
```

Each mount leaks an open channel that keeps receiving messages after unmount.

## Edge cases

- Unclonable messages (functions, DOM nodes) → `postMessage` returns `false` and `onError` fires.
- Other hook instances in the same tab do receive the message.

## Browser support

Feature-detected (`isSupported`); `false` on the server.

- Version your message types; old tabs can stay open for days.
